newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Infometrics wants output stability in RBNZ aims.
newsitem.headline: Infometrics wants output stability in RBNZ aims.

text.p: Economic forecaster Infometrics wants the Reserve Bank Act changed so it includes a requirement to take account of objectives other than price stability.
In a paper "Monetary and Fiscal Policy -- Two Part Harmony?" economists Philip Wrigley and Gareth Morgan argued that output stability should be specifically included in the Reserve Bank's objectives.
"The bank is doing this is practice so, for the sake of transparency, it should be stated in the RB Act," the economists said.

They argued the bank has a formal output goal in the policy targets agreement (between the bank's governor and the minister of finance) through its ability to exclude large price movements such as an oil shock or an increase in goods and services tax.
But it also has a de facto output goal evidenced by its October 1995 decision to ease when it saw output trending sharply lower and expected inflation to follow.
In October 1995, inflation was two percent with "negligible prospect of it falling below one percent let alone zero," the economists said.

"It was releasing some pressure on economic output in a trade-off against zero inflation. Yet so long as inflation is in the target zone, the Act doesn't stipulate the trade-off should be made," they said.
They said monetary policy through the Reserve Bank Act and fiscal policy through the Fiscal Responsibility Act needed to be co-ordinated, but the independence of the Reserve Bank should be preserved.

The government should signal well in advance economic policy changes which influence monetary conditions. If these changes breach the support of monetary policy it should be done in full knowledge of the consequences.

"Having made such a political decision, the Reserve Bank must support the government by juggling its price stability objective against excessive output costs that would result from continuous price stability."
They said this framework would allow the bank to remain independent but accept a wider role than the "pure pursuit of continuous price stability as is happening in practice now in 1996."

They said with this practice in place there would be no need for the Act's provision for the Finance Minister to override the price stability objective. It would also make the policy targets agreement unnecessary.
The focus then would be on maintaining stable prices on average over the medium term rather than maintain "a narrow target for the year ending in each 13 week period as at present."

They said change was needed and would occur, but if left unattended, tensions in the present system would lead to a crisis-driven change which could compromise progress New Zealand has made towards price stability.
